request.title: Add an undo command
request.body: Add a command, undo, that reverses the most recent add, done or remove made on the store. It replies with what it reversed and the id of the task: "Undid add 3", "Undid done 2" or "Undid remove 1". Undoing an add takes the task out of the list; its id is still never given to another task. Undoing done marks the task as not done again. Undoing remove puts the task back in the place in the list it had before, with the same id, title and done mark. undo can be used again and again to step further back, one command at a time. When there is nothing left to reverse it replies "Nothing to undo." A command that fails with an error, and the list command, change nothing and are not something undo reverses. Everything that works today must keep working. Plain ES modules, no dependencies.

artifact.title: Add an undo command to the task store tool
artifact.problem: The task store's add, done and remove operations are one-way. A user who runs one of them by mistake, or changes their mind, has no way to back it out: they must counteract it by hand, and a removed task's id, title, done mark and place in the list cannot be restored that way at all. There is no safe, step-by-step way to reverse a recent change.
goals: Provide an undo command that reverses the most recent successful add, done or remove on the store, exactly one action per invocation.
Reply with what was reversed and the id of the affected task, using the exact wording 'Undid add <id>', 'Undid done <id>' or 'Undid remove <id>'.
Let the user step further back by running undo again and again, one action at a time.
Reply 'Nothing to undo.' and change nothing when there is no reversible action left.
Keep ids unique for good: an id whose add is undone is never given to another task.
Keep every existing command working exactly as it does today.
nonGoals: No redo command: re-applying a reversed action, or undoing an undo, is out of scope; a user who wants the work back can run the normal commands again.
Only add, done and remove become reversible; making any other command reversible is out of scope.
No multi-step, selective or named undo: undo always reverses the single most recent reversible action, and the user cannot choose which one.
No changes to the names, arguments, replies or effects of existing commands.
No new interface beyond the command itself; nothing visual or interactive is added.
constraints: Plain ES modules; no new dependencies or tooling.
Undo's replies are fixed strings: 'Undid add <id>', 'Undid done <id>', 'Undid remove <id>' and 'Nothing to undo.'.
All behavior that exists today must keep working unchanged.

The request does not say whether the record of past actions must survive a restart or reload of the store; these requirements are stated in terms of the actions recorded on the store and prescribe no particular way of keeping that record.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When the most recent successful action on the store is an add that created the task with id N, running undo replies 'Undid add N', and that task no longer appears when the tasks are listed.
When the most recent successful action on the store is a done that marked the task with id N as done, running undo replies 'Undid done N', and that task is no longer marked done.

When the most recent successful action on the store is a remove that took the task with id N out of the list, running undo replies 'Undid remove N', and the task appears in the list again, in the place it occupied before the removal relative to the tasks still present, with the same id N, the same title and the same done mark it had when it was removed.

Each undo invocation reverses exactly one action: the most recent successful add, done or remove not yet reversed. Run in sequence, undo reverses actions in the opposite order to the one in which they happened; for example, after an add, a done and a remove on the same task, successive undo invocations reply 'Undid remove N', then 'Undid done N', then 'Undid add N'.

Running undo when no successful add, done or remove is left to reverse, for example on a store where none has ever happened or after every one has already been undone, replies 'Nothing to undo.' and changes nothing in the store.
After undoing the add of the task with id N, no later add ever produces a task with id N: every task added afterwards receives a different id, and id N is never used again.

A command that fails with an error is not something undo reverses: after a failed command, running undo reverses the most recent successful add, done or remove from before the failure, or replies 'Nothing to undo.' if there was none.

The list command is not something undo reverses: after running list, running undo reverses the most recent successful add, done or remove from before it, or replies 'Nothing to undo.' if there was none.

Every command that works before this change still works the same way afterwards: for the same store contents and the same arguments, each existing command produces the same reply and the same effect on the store as it did before the change.

artifact.approach: Give the store a private, in-memory undo stack. Each successful add, complete and remove pushes a small inverse record captured at mutation time: add records the new id; complete records the id and the task's done value before it was set to true; remove records the id, title, done mark and the task's index in the list. A new store method undo() pops the top record and reverses it exactly, returning {type, id} or null when the stack is empty. A new 'undo' case in cli.js maps that result to the fixed replies 'Undid add N', 'Undid done N', 'Undid remove N' or 'Nothing to undo.'. No existing behavior changes: the only edit to add/complete/remove is pushing a record after the mutation succeeds, and id allocation stays monotonic, so an undone add's id is never reissued (AC-6 already follows from the existing nextId counter, which never decreases).

components.name: Undo history in the store
components.responsibility: Record every successful add, done and remove on the store as a reversible entry, and reverse the most recent unreversed entry on demand, restoring task fields and list position exactly.

components.name: Undo command in the CLI
components.responsibility: Dispatch the 'undo' command to store.undo() and turn its result into the fixed reply strings, without touching any existing command.

interfaces.contract: Exports createStore() as today. The returned store keeps an in-memory task list with ids starting at 1 that are never reused; the id counter never decreases, including when a task is removed or an add is undone. Public methods: add(title) trims String(title ?? '') and throws Error('A task needs a title') when empty, otherwise creates {id, title, done:false}, appends it, and returns a copy — unchanged for callers. complete(id) throws Error('No task with id <id>') when absent, otherwise captures the task's done value, sets done=true, and returns a copy — unchanged for callers. remove(id) throws the same error when absent, otherwise splices the task out and returns undefined — unchanged for callers. all() returns copies of every task in order — unchanged. NEW method undo(): pops the most recent recorded, not-yet-reversed action and reverses it in place; 'add' deletes the task with the recorded id from the list; 'done' sets that task's done back to the captured prior value; 'remove' re-inserts a task with the recorded id, title and done at the recorded list index, clamped with Math.min(index, tasks.length). Returns a fresh object {type, id} with type one of 'add', 'done', 'remove', or null when no reversible action remains; when it returns null the store is unchanged. undo() records nothing itself (no redo). Each of add, complete and remove records its entry only after the mutation succeeds, so failures leave the stack untouched.

Exports run(args, store) with the same signature. add, done, remove and list behave exactly as today, including their replies ('Added <id>: <title>', 'Completed <id>', 'Removed <id>', formatList(store.all())) and their errors (Error('Not a task id: <text>') and Error('Unknown command: <command ?? "(none)">')). NEW case 'undo': accepts no arguments (extra arguments are ignored, as with list); calls store.undo(); when it returns null, returns 'Nothing to undo.'; otherwise returns `Undid ${result.type} ${result.id}`, producing exactly 'Undid add N', 'Undid done N' or 'Undid remove N'. The doc comment listing the commands gains a line for undo.

decisions.title: History lives inside the store, not the CLI
decisions.decision: createStore() owns a private array of inverse records; cli.js only calls store.undo() and formats the reply.
decisions.rationale: The store already owns all mutation and the CLI is a thin dispatcher; keeping the record next to the tasks means every mutation site is the single place that knows what reversal needs, and list or unknown commands cannot touch the history (AC-8).

decisions.title: LIFO stack of minimal inverse records
decisions.decision: Each successful action pushes one record: add → {type:'add', id}; complete → {type:'done', id, done:<prior value>}; remove → {type:'remove', id, title, done, index}. undo() pops exactly one and applies the inverse.
decisions.rationale: Undoing one action per call in reverse order is exactly AC-4, and capturing the prior done value and the list index at mutation time is the only way to restore a removed task's mark and position per AC-3 without guessing.

decisions.title: undo() returns a descriptor or null, not a string and not an error
decisions.decision: store.undo() returns {type, id} for what it reversed, or null when the stack is empty; the CLI renders the fixed strings.
decisions.rationale: 'Nothing to undo.' is a normal reply, not a failure (AC-5), so it must not throw; the store stays free of UI wording, matching the existing split where cli.js builds replies and format.js renders lists.

decisions.title: Record labels use the command names
decisions.decision: The type field uses 'done' (not 'complete'), alongside 'add' and 'remove', so the reply is the direct template `Undid ${type} ${id}`.
decisions.rationale: The required wording is 'Undid done N'; naming the record after the command removes any mapping layer and keeps the fixed strings verbatim.

decisions.title: No change to id allocation
decisions.decision: Leave nextId monotonic and never decrement it, including when undoing an add.
decisions.rationale: AC-6 is already guaranteed by the existing counter, which only increments; undoing an add removes the task while nextId stays past its id, so no later add can reuse it.

decisions.title: Failures record nothing, with no wrapper needed
decisions.decision: Push each record only after the mutation succeeds; keep the existing throw-first structure in add, complete and remove.
decisions.rationale: All three already validate before mutating, so a failed command leaves the stack and the store untouched, which is exactly AC-7.

decisions.title: History is in memory and per store instance
decisions.decision: The undo stack is a closure variable in createStore(), with no persistence.
decisions.rationale: The store is in-memory today and the constraints deliberately prescribe no particular way of keeping the record; a closure-local stack is the smallest design that meets the criteria.

decisions.title: undo ignores extra arguments
decisions.decision: run(['undo', ...anything], store) behaves like run(['undo'], store).
decisions.rationale: Matches how the existing list command ignores arguments, keeps the dispatcher uniform, and the requirements give undo no arguments.

risks: The undo stack grows without bound in a long-lived store instance; a cap would violate AC-4, so this is accepted, but it is worth remembering if the store ever becomes long-lived or shared.

The design relies on every mutating store method recording an entry: a future mutation that bypasses the stack would break the LIFO invariant and could make an undone 'done' reference a task that no longer exists. Any new mutating method must record or the invariant must be revisited.
Restore-by-index is exact under the LIFO discipline; the Math.min clamp is only a guard, so a test asserting position restoration should rely on the recorded index, not on the clamp.

The fixed reply strings are templated straight from the record's type field, so renaming 'done' or the other labels would silently change the user-facing wording; the labels are part of the contract and must not drift.

reason: the work has no user interface

findings.comment: Not a defect, just a robustness note: in undo(), the 'add' and 'done' branches silently no-op when the recorded task is no longer in the list (index === -1 / !task) while still returning a success descriptor, so a future mutation that bypasses the history stack (the LIFO-invariant risk the architecture itself flags) would be masked rather than surfaced. Today those states are unreachable under strict LIFO, so the behavior is correct against every AC; if you ever want the invariant enforced, throwing or asserting there would make violations visible. No change required.

artifact.title: Add an undo command that reverses the most recent add, done or remove
artifact.summary: The store's add, done and remove were one-way: a mistaken or regretted action had to be counteracted by hand, and a removed task's id, title, done mark and position could not be restored at all. This change adds an undo command that reverses the single most recent successful add, done or remove, replying 'Undid add <id>', 'Undid done <id>' or 'Undid remove <id>', or 'Nothing to undo.' when nothing reversible remains; running it repeatedly steps back one action at a time, most recent first. An id whose add was undone is never reissued, and no existing command's name, arguments, replies or effects change. Test coverage is documented for all nine acceptance criteria (AC-1 through AC-9). Reviewers should start with undo() and the three history push sites in src/store.js — in particular that a remove captures the list index before splicing, that records are pushed only after a mutation succeeds, the Math.min(recorded index, tasks.length) clamp on remove restore, and that nextId is never decremented — then the small 'undo' case in src/cli.js.
changes: src/store.js — createStore() gains a private, closure-local undo history and a new public undo() method; the signatures, validation, errors and return values of add(), complete(), remove() and all() are unchanged. Each successful mutation pushes one minimal inverse record only after it succeeds: add pushes {type:'add', id}; complete captures the task's done value before setting it and pushes {type:'done', id, done:<prior value>}; remove captures the task's list index at the moment it is spliced out and pushes {type:'remove', id, title, done, index}. Failed commands throw before any push, so they leave the history and the store untouched, and all()/list record nothing. undo() pops exactly one record and reverses it in place: an add deletes the task with the recorded id, a done restores the captured prior done value, and a remove re-inserts a task with the recorded id, title and done at Math.min(recorded index, tasks.length). It returns a fresh {type, id} object with type exactly 'add', 'done' or 'remove', or null on an empty history, in which case the store is unchanged. undo() records nothing itself (no redo), and nextId is never decremented, so an undone add's id is never reissued.

src/cli.js — run(args, store) gains an 'undo' case. It takes no arguments (extras are ignored, as with list), calls store.undo(), returns 'Nothing to undo.' when the result is null, and otherwise returns `Undid ${result.type} ${result.id}`, yielding exactly 'Undid add N', 'Undid done N' or 'Undid remove N'. The doc comment's command list gains a line for undo. No other command, reply, argument handling or error path was touched.

Tests — documented coverage maps every acceptance criterion to one or more cases: the three undo replies and their store effects (AC-1–AC-3), one-action-per-invocation reversal in the opposite order to the original actions (AC-4), 'Nothing to undo.' with no change to the store when nothing is left to reverse (AC-5), no id reuse after an undone add (AC-6), failed commands recording nothing for undo, including when no successful action preceded them (AC-7), list recording nothing (AC-8), and unchanged replies, effects and errors for existing commands, including after undo has been used (AC-9).
risks: The undo history lives only in memory, closure-local to the store instance: it does not survive a restart or reload. After the store is re-created, undo replies 'Nothing to undo.' even for un-undone actions from before. The PRD deliberately leaves whether the record must persist unspecified, so this is a permitted boundary, but it is the main behavioral limit to sign off on — and if task data persists anywhere while the history does not, undo will only ever see the current session's actions.

The history grows without bound: every successful add, done or remove pushes a record, and only undo pops one. There is no cap or pruning, so a long-lived store instance accumulates records indefinitely; the records are small, but confirm that is acceptable.

If complete() can succeed on a task that is already done, the pushed record captures the prior done value of true, and undoing that invocation would reply 'Undid done <id>' while leaving the task still done. The artifacts do not state whether complete() succeeds or throws in that case — worth a quick check that the reply semantics there are intended.
